nodes.title: SG-7.1 · Add the worker Go module with config, logger, file lock and JSON store
nodes.body:
Context: no worker module exists in the workspace (the repo holds only backend/, game/ and context.md). SG-7 needs a foundation for the execution runner. Desired behavior: a separate Go module at backend/worker with a YAML config loader, a JSON structured logger, an exclusive file lock and a JSON execution store. Expected result: each piece builds and has unit-testable behavior. Why: the runner can then be built on top of these primitives.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a YAML file, when worker config LoadFS runs, then defaults are filled and STORYFORGE_WORKER_* env values override YAML values
- Given a logger built with a level, when a record is logged, then one JSON line is written containing msg and level
- Given a held lock file, when a second Acquire runs on the same path, then it fails with ErrLocked until Release is called
- Given an execution, when Save then Get run on the store, then the same record is returned and unsafe ids are rejected


## Scope
- In scope: backend/worker module with go.mod
- In scope: config loader
- In scope: slog JSON logger
- In scope: file lock
- In scope: JSON execution store
- Out of scope: runner, providers, poller and git operations
- Out of scope: changes to the backend module
- Preserve: existing backend module and its tests


## Technical constraints
- Go, YAML via gopkg.in/yaml.v3, stdlib log/slog
- No database; state is JSON files on the local filesystem
- Module path github.com/worldseed/storyforge/worker


## Definition of done
- All four packages build with go build ./... inside backend/worker


## Non-functional requirements
- Execution ids are path-traversal safe


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Worker module loads YAML config with defaults and env overrides
nodes.body:
Context: backend/internal/config/config.go has the LoadFS(fsys, name, getenv) pattern; the worker has none. Desired behavior: backend/worker module exposes config.LoadFS with the same shape. Expected result: a validated Config for the worker. Why: the runner needs configured paths and timeouts.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a YAML file with only worker.repo_path, when LoadFS runs, then PollInterval is 30s, ExecutionTimeout is 30m, MaxRetries is 2 and Store.Dir is .storyforge/executions
- Given STORYFORGE_WORKER_REPO_PATH is set, when LoadFS runs, then it overrides the YAML repo_path
- Given an empty repo_path after env overrides, when LoadFS runs, then it returns an error


## Scope
- In scope: backend/worker/go.mod
- In scope: config package
- In scope: config.example.yaml
- Out of scope: runner wiring
- Preserve: backend/internal/config unchanged


## Technical constraints
- Mirror the LoadFS(fsys fs.FS, name string, getenv func(string) string) signature of the backend config


## Definition of done
- config package builds and example YAML parses


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Worker writes structured JSON logs at a configured level
nodes.body:
Context: backend uses slog.NewJSONHandler inline in cmd/server/main.go; the worker needs a reusable factory. Desired behavior: logging.New(w, level) returns a JSON slog logger. Expected result: parseable log lines filtered by level. Why: execution reports need structured logs.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given level info, when Info is logged, then one JSON line with msg and level INFO is written
- Given level warn, when Info is logged, then nothing is written
- Given an unknown level string, when New runs, then it returns an error

- In scope: logging package
- Out of scope: log file rotation
- Preserve: backend logging


## Technical constraints
- stdlib log/slog only

nodes.title: REQ · Worker holds an exclusive file lock so only one runs per World
nodes.body:
Context: the worker must run one execution per World at a time. Desired behavior: lock.Acquire(path) creates the lock file exclusively and Release removes it. Expected result: a second Acquire returns ErrLocked. Why: prevents concurrent executions.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given no lock file, when Acquire runs, then it succeeds and the file contains the pid
- Given a held lock, when Acquire runs again, then it returns an error satisfying errors.Is(err, ErrLocked)
- Given Release was called, when Acquire runs again, then it succeeds


## Scope
- In scope: lock package
- Out of scope: stale-lock recovery


## Technical constraints
- os.OpenFile with O_CREATE|O_EXCL; no external dependencies


## Dependencies
- R1 module go.mod


## Definition of done
- lock package builds


## Non-functional requirements
- Release is idempotent


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Executions persist as atomically written JSON records with safe ids
nodes.body:
Context: no persistence exists for worker executions. Desired behavior: store.Store saves one <id>.json per Execution via temp file and rename. Expected result: round-trip persistence and rejection of ids like ../x. Why: recovery after restart needs durable state.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given an Execution, when Save then Get run, then the returned record equals the saved one
- Given three saved executions, when List runs, then all three are returned sorted by ID
- Given id ../evil, when Save or Get runs, then ErrInvalidID is returned and no file is written outside the dir
- Given an unknown id, when Get runs, then ErrNotFound is returned


## Scope
- In scope: store package
- Out of scope: startup recovery logic


## Technical constraints
- JSON files only; ids must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ and not contain ..


## Dependencies
- R1 module go.mod


## Definition of done
- store package builds


## Non-functional requirements
- Writes are atomic via rename


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: Add var ErrLocked = errors.New("lock: already held"); type Lock struct{path string; released bool}; Acquire(path string) (*Lock, error): os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path),0o755), os.OpenFile(path, O_CREATE|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY, 0o600); on errors.Is(err, fs.ErrExist) return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrLocked, path); write strconv.Itoa(os.Getpid()) and close. nodes.summary: Add store.Store with Save, Get, List and id validation
nodes.description: Implement atomic JSON persistence of executions.
acceptance_criteria: Save is atomic
Invalid ids are rejected

steps.symbol: new: Execution, Status consts, Store, New
steps.action: Define type Status string with consts StatusPending, StatusRunning, StatusAwaitingApproval, StatusCompleted, StatusFailed; Execution{ID, RoundID string; Status Status; Attempt int; Error string; CreatedAt, UpdatedAt time.Time} with json tags id, round_id, status, attempt, error, created_at, updated_at; type Store struct{dir string}; New(dir string) *Store; vars ErrInvalidID, ErrNotFound.

Validate e.ID against regexp ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ and reject ids containing '..' returning ErrInvalidID; MkdirAll(dir); json.MarshalIndent e; write to os.CreateTemp(dir, '.tmp-*'), close, os.Rename to dir/<id>.json.

Get(id) validates id, reads dir/<id>.json, returns ErrNotFound on fs.ErrNotExist, json.Unmarshal into Execution. List() reads dir entries ending in .json (empty slice when dir missing), loads each via Get and returns them sorted by ID with sort.Slice.

func (s *Store) List() ([]Execution, error)
steps.expected: Round-trip returns identical records, sorted by ID
